facts: The claim for air ambulance services is not covered under your policy.
The treating Medical Practitioner did not certify in writing that the severity or the nature of the Insured Person's Illness or Injury warranted the requirement for Air Ambulance services.

cited_clauses.quote: Air Ambulance cover The Company will indemnify the Insured Person up to the amount as specified in Policy Schedule , for the Reasonable and Customary Charges necessarily incurred on availing Air Ambulance services, in India, offered by a Hospital or by an Ambulance service provider for the Insured Person's necessary transportation, provided that: The treating Medical Practitioner certifies in writing that the severity or the nature of the Insured Person's Illness or Injury warrants the Insured Person's requirement for Air Ambulance;
The treating Medical Practitioner certifies in writing that the severity or the nature of the Insured Person's Illness or Injury warrants the Insured Person's requirement for Air Ambulance;

reasoning: The policy clause requires a written certification from the treating Medical Practitioner, which was missing in this case.
relief_sought: We request the insurer to reconsider the claim and cover the air ambulance services as they are necessary for the Insured Person's medical condition.
document_checklist: Copy of the claim rejection letter
Medical bills, prescriptions and investigation reports
Earlier correspondence with the insurer, including any grievance acknowledgement
deadline_note: A complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman needs a written representation to the insurer first; it must then be made within one year of the insurer's rejection, or of one month after the representation was sent (Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, Rule 14(3), checked against the published text as amended till 09.11.2023; later amendments not checked). Confirm with the Ombudsman office before relying on a date, and compute dates with the deadline tool.
